aula-plenary-1-01-tdwg-chair-address-ope.title: Opening of TDWG 2026 and welcome to Oslo
aula-plenary-1-01-tdwg-chair-address-ope.description: David Bloom opens the conference and polls the room. Hugo de Boer then welcomes everyone to Oslo, from Munch's paintings in the Aula and the troll logo to the week's excursions and evening events.

aula-taster-01-kearney-bhl-opening.title: Taste of TDWG
aula-taster-01-kearney-bhl-opening.description: Ellie Wallace explains how the taster talks were chosen to sample the themes that emerged around research- and robot-ready data standards.

odin-2026-09-22-01-opening.title: Building resilient data infrastructures for biodiversity science
odin-2026-09-22-01-opening.description: The co-chairs set out why resilience matters now: funding cuts, AI crawlers putting portals under pressure, and datasets decommissioned for political reasons.

odin-2026-09-22-09-opening.title: Data Quality: From Standard to Practice
odin-2026-09-22-09-opening.description: Lee Belbin gives a status update on the Biodiversity Data Quality standard: expert review is done, public review is next, and it will bring TDWG's first ontology.

sala-2026-09-22-20-opening.title: BHL at 20: A New Chapter for Biodiversity Literature and Data - Transforming BHL: Data Extraction, Semantic Navigation and Future Interfaces
sala-2026-09-22-20-opening.description: David Iggulden and Nicole Kearney recap the first BHL session and introduce the talks on data extraction, semantic navigation and future interfaces.

salc-2026-09-22-01-opening.title: Rocks, Minerals, and Metadata: Integrating Earth Sciences into the TDWG Community
salc-2026-09-22-01-opening.description: Standing in for Ben Norton, Adam Mansur presents the strategy for bringing geological collections into TDWG, from GeoSpecify to the mineralogy extension and the GeoSpecimens portal.

forum-2026-09-24-22-opening.title: From WDSRPD to GeoSchemes: Recording Biodiversity Distributions for Science and Policy
forum-2026-09-24-22-opening.description: Paco Pando explains why the plant-only geographical scheme (WGSRPD) is being replaced by one that covers land and sea for every taxon.

sala-2026-09-24-01-opening.title: From Cabinets to Clouds - Bridging the gap between collection- and database management
sala-2026-09-24-01-opening.description: Nora Lentge-Maaß introduces the Berlin organisers and the symposium's aim: learning how institutions connect physical collections with digital data workflows, and who is responsible for what.

sala-2026-09-24-13-opening.title: Solutions for Research Collection Management Systems Challenges
sala-2026-09-24-13-opening.description: James Macklin explains the focus on research: helping researchers manage their own data to standards so it can be integrated with other data.

salb-2026-09-24-16-opening.title: A consensus taxonomic reference for improved freshwater biodiversity data and knowledge
salb-2026-09-24-16-opening.description: Astrid Schmidt-Kloiber introduces the co-organisers and the freshwater paradox: tiny in area but rich in biodiversity, with data that deserve special attention.

salc-2026-09-24-10-opening.title: From Mobilizing Data to AI-Ready Knowledge: Infrastructure for Multimodal Biodiversity Data
salc-2026-09-24-10-opening.description: Hilmar Lapp lists why biodiversity data are often not AI-ready: buried knowledge, inconsistent documentation, weak interoperability, hard-to-judge fitness for use, broken provenance and unclear terms of use.

sala-2026-09-25-01-opening.title: Large Language Models for Biodiversity Data Discovery, Integration, and Curation. Part A: AI- enabled knowledge creation and extraction
sala-2026-09-25-01-opening.description: Yasin Bakış frames the session's questions: can LLMs extract biodiversity information reliably, with provenance, uncertainty and links to standards, and where do humans stay involved?

salc-2026-09-25-07-opening.title: From Standards to Implementation: Connecting Observation Data in Asia to GBIF Infrastructure
salc-2026-09-25-07-opening.description: Kumiko Totsu introduces case studies from Asia on managing and publishing observation data, aimed at small teams with limited resources.
